newsitem.title: GERMANY: ICE train no threat to Transrapid - Deutsche Bahn.
newsitem.headline: ICE train no threat to Transrapid - Deutsche Bahn.

text.p: The German railway said on Monday the introduction of high-speed Inter-City Express (ICE) trains between Berlin and Hamburg this year was no threat to plans to link the cities with a controversial magnetic levitation train.

The ICE, which is due to begin on the Berlin- Hamburg route July 1, "is an important step on the way to the Transrapid," Heinz Neuhaus, passenger traffic chief at Deutsche Bahn AG, said at a tourism industry conference.
ICE traffic would help create the necessary demand for high-speed rail links between the two northern German cities, he said.

After Deutsche Bahn completes track improvements, an ICE train should be able to make the trip in about two hours and 15 minutes, travelling at a top speed of 280 kilometers per hour, Neuhaus said. The Transrapid, travelling up to 420 km/h, would cover the trip in about an hour.
The trip now takes two hours and 45 minutes on tracks built for a maximum speed of 160 km/h, Neuhaus said.

Critics of the Transrapid have said the estimated nine billion mark project is too high to allow for affordable ticket prices. The project is backed by Deutsche Bahn, Siemens AG, Thyssen AG and ADtranz.
Construction of the Transrapid is expected to begin in 1998, with operations beginning in 2005.
